en: The Philippine eagle is the only eagle with a shaggy crest of dark brown feathers on its head, making it look like it has wild hair.
Emilio Aguinaldo was only 29 years old when he proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The Philippine Senate is the only government body that can try and convict an impeached official, acting as a special impeachment court.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian admitted to Harvard Medical School and later invented a makeshift incubator using two native bamboo baskets.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces over 2,000 years ago by carving the mountains entirely by hand without using any modern machines.
The Philippine language Eskayan has its own unique alphabet of over 1,000 characters that was created to look like human body parts.
Apolinario Mabini lost the use of both legs to polio but still directed the Philippine revolution while being carried in a bamboo hammock.
The Giant Lantern Festival in San Fernando features massive, spinning parol lanterns that use thousands of individually wired, blinking light bulbs.
The Philippine Constitution grants citizens the unique right to a balanced and healthful ecology, making environmental protection a guaranteed legal right.
The national flower, Sampaguita, is a native jasmine that only releases its sweet fragrance during the night to attract specific pollinating moths.
The traditional Bayanihan practice literally involves an entire community carrying a native nipa hut on bamboo poles to relocate it for a neighbor.
National Artist Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the famous Bonifacio Monument using 16 different real Filipinos as his physical models for the carved figures.
